      "startEvent": 1447,
      "endEvent": 1450,
      "contextStartEvent": 1438,
      "contextEndEvent": 1468,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "if you can't give an answer to that that i'm skeptical of whether your view is an evidence-based view",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B suggests that inability to specify convincing evidence casts doubt on A's evidential openness. He does not establish why evaluating offered evidence requires designing a successful alternative test. This could discount criticism through an alleged methodological defect, but E1438–E1447 also permits an ordinary request for standards; disagreement alone is not declared disqualifying."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1787,
      "endEvent": 1796,
      "contextStartEvent": 1749,
      "contextEndEvent": 1796,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "that's fine um that comes down to how flawed your epistemology is",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A characterizes acceptance as a defect in reasoning, potentially insulating his assessment by diagnosing the believer. However, E1789–E1792 specifically imagines someone accepting evidence they concede is not strong, and E1749–E1786 supplies objections about sources and investigation. The passage does not clearly establish that any opposing assessment proves a defect."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2358,
      "endEvent": 2369,
      "contextStartEvent": 2280,
      "contextEndEvent": 2375,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it's invoked only to only to get around the hypothesis of truth",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "B attributes an evasive purpose to the shared-tradition alternative without establishing that motive. This could dismiss a criticism independently of its merits. Yet E2344–E2364 also offers a substantive objection about interlocking separate stories, and E2301–E2317 restricts which variations support independence. An unrestricted every-outcome-confirms device is not established."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2434,
      "endEvent": 2438,
      "contextStartEvent": 2393,
      "contextEndEvent": 2485,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "i will never ever accept that as a good reason to believe that somebody was raised from the dead",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The categorical refusal could exclude testimony before considering its merits. However, 'that' refers to trusting otherwise trustworthy authors, and E2393–E2433 supplies reasons involving shared stories and honest error. E3822–E3867 later accepts contextual testimony as a data point, making blanket protection against all testimonial counterevidence uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2456,
      "endEvent": 2461,
      "contextStartEvent": 2434,
      "contextEndEvent": 2485,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "for resurrection our priors are not minimal they're zero",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Taken literally, a zero prior blocks later evidence from raising the probability, while absence of verified examples does not establish impossibility. E2458–E2461 invokes missing evidence, suggesting 'zero' might mean no established precedents. E4001–E4027 explicitly allows sufficient evidence to establish resurrection, so a permanent protective use remains uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3360,
      "endEvent": 3366,
      "contextStartEvent": 3270,
      "contextEndEvent": 3380,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "that's an abductive argument which is the weakest form of argument",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The compact ranking dismisses inference to the best explanation through its category without supplying a reason that this form is invariably weakest. E3360–E3364 explains the category identification, not the ranking. B had distinguished reliability reasoning from alternative-explanation reasoning at E3193–E3289; A's surrounding methodological objections do not establish this general hierarchy."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3519,
      "endEvent": 3526,
      "contextStartEvent": 3505,
      "contextEndEvent": 3526,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "any other historical book that was making claims about supernatural events i would reject those as well",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "A states a general exclusion that could protect his position from historical counterevidence. In context he answers an accusation of unequal standards, with earlier reasons about testimony and corroboration. E4001–E4027 subsequently distinguishes establishing an event from explaining its cause and explicitly allows sufficient evidence to convince him; blanket exclusion is therefore uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3910,
      "endEvent": 3919,
      "contextStartEvent": 3822,
      "contextEndEvent": 3937,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the plural of anecdote isn't data",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The maxim does inferential work against accumulating testimony, without separately establishing why multiple reports cannot add evidential weight. However, E3913–E3915 specifies anonymous reports, and E3822–E3909 explains contextual reliability and background evidence. It may summarize objections to these reports rather than categorically exclude all testimonial accumulation; E4262–E4268 also concedes comparative evidential improvement."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 4001,
      "endEvent": 4034,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "if there was sufficient evidence for the resurrection i would believe the resurrection occurred",
      "explanation": "A distinguishes evidence that an event occurred from evidence explaining its cause at E4014–E4027. This explicitly qualified willingness to revise is informative against reading his earlier categorical language as an unconditional refusal of resurrection evidence."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 3650,
      "endEvent": 3663,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "then that would reduce my confidence correspondingly in the resurrection",
      "explanation": "B identifies weakening of his supporting arguments as a reason to reduce confidence, after acknowledging the practical problem with identifying Jesus's body. E3689–E3717 adds inconsistent evidential standards and accumulating contrary evidence as further revision conditions."
    }
  ]
